title: A record Nvidia quarter fails to stop a 10% weekly rout in AI hardware as an SEC probe and new export rules weigh
intro: Nvidia reported a record quarter and guided higher, but a reported SEC civil probe into its disclosures and the new US curbs on AI compute access kept selling pressure on the whole chain, and Friday's slide in AI picks-and-shovels stocks pushed the Nasdaq negative for the year. Anthropic's IPO priced and debuted in the middle of it, while packaging, substrates and neocloud names took the heaviest losses.
movers_note: Against the Monday Nov 16 close the tracked total fell 10.23% to $24.18T over the week (ASML's market cap on the source fell about $26B less than its price implied), and it is down 14.28% from the Nov 13 close a week earlier; all 62 companies fell, with SK hynix (−0.6%), Zhongji Innolight (−3.9%), Foxconn (−3.9%), Amazon (−4.2%) and Quanta Services (−4.6%) holding up best and Nan Ya PCB (−28.5%), Nebius (−24.1%), Unimicron (−24.0%), CoreWeave (−20.8%) and ASE (−19.9%) falling most.

items.headline: Nvidia posts a $115.8B quarter and guides to $130B, excluding China data-center sales
items.summary: Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter revenue more than doubled from a year earlier to $115.8B, with data-center revenue of $107.6B, up 110%. It guided the next quarter to $130.0B plus or minus 3%, assumes no China data-center compute revenue, and said Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are now shipping.

items.headline: SEC reportedly opens a civil probe into Nvidia's disclosures after Huang's exit
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the SEC is investigating whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors, with questions centered on Asia and Jensen Huang's ties to an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is suspected of rerouting chips to China. California's attorney general said his office is also weighing whether action is warranted.

items.headline: AI picks-and-shovels selloff drags the Nasdaq negative for the year
items.summary: Nvidia fell almost 10% at one point on Friday, heading for a seventh straight weekly loss and down 33% in November, as reports of SEC scrutiny weighed. Micron lost about 12%, CoreWeave almost 11% and Bloom Energy more than 12% intraday as the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026.

items.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share and lists on Nasdaq
items.summary: Anthropic priced 980 million Class A shares at $83.00, about 956.4 million of them sold by the company and the rest by existing holders, with underwriters holding an option on up to 147 million more. Trading under the ticker ANT was set to begin on Nov 19.

items.headline: New US export rules narrow license exemptions for foundries and packaging houses
items.summary: TrendForce says the tightened BIS rules cut back export-license exemptions for foundries and OSATs, so TSMC, Samsung, ASE and Amkor may face stricter customer checks that could delay orders from Chinese designers. TSMC said it is reviewing the rules; suppliers see first-half 2027 orders as largely secured but second-half visibility as uncertain.

items.headline: Nvidia's networking business tops $21B a quarter as cloud backlog reaches $2.5T
items.summary: On the earnings call Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress put third-quarter networking revenue above $21B and the cloud industry backlog at $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion three months earlier. She tied the next-quarter outlook to a strong Vera Rubin ramp, with Vera Rubin Ultra due next year.

items.headline: TrendForce sees DRAM contract prices still rising but with shrinking gains
items.summary: TrendForce expects DRAM contract prices to keep climbing with smaller increases each quarter, as mobile DRAM talks stall and spot demand stays weak. HBM procurement is largely locked in, while new capacity from the three big suppliers is narrowing the shortage.
